recipes.purpose: Show a before-and-after change in one named quantity for one shared scope.
recipes.data: Exactly 2 labeled numeric values with measure.quantity, matching scope, and explicit periods.

recipes.purpose: Compare actual, expected, target, or alternative values of one named quantity for one shared scope and period.
recipes.data: 2 to 5 labeled numeric values with measure.quantity and matching scope and period. A two-item standalone chart also needs a numeric reference, basis, or source-supported mechanism, consequence, denominator, or comparison fact; otherwise enrich, merge, or omit it.

recipes.purpose: Compare small-to-medium exact counts with one visible symbol per unit so extreme count ratios remain tangible.
recipes.data: 2 to 4 labeled non-negative integer values from 0 to 400 with measure.quantity and matching scope and period.

recipes.purpose: Compare positive and negative changes in one named quantity for one shared scope and period.
recipes.data: 2 to 10 labeled numeric changes with measure.quantity and matching scope and period; values may be positive or negative.

recipes.purpose: Show exact values, min-max intervals, and thresholds for one named quantity on one scale.
recipes.data: 1 to 8 items with value or low/high fields, measure.quantity, and matching scope and period. A single interval requires a visible benchmark or reference that supplies the total or threshold scale.

recipes.purpose: Show an actual value as part of a benchmark total so the discount, premium, shortfall, or overage remains visible.
recipes.data: 1 to 6 labeled items with an underlying actual value and benchmark total in one unit, plus matching quantity and scope. Use one item when the benchmark and its implied gap fully carry the story.

recipes.purpose: Visualize two differently measured factors converging on one outcome without forcing them onto a shared axis.
recipes.data: Exactly 3 items: two relationshipRole driver items and one outcome item. Every item needs a value or range, direction, displayValue, quantity, scope, and period. Each item is drawn on its own local quantitative signal; connectors encode the relationship, not comparable magnitude.

recipes.purpose: Compare two values for several categories while preserving the direction and size of every category-level change.
recipes.data: 3 to 10 labeled items with value and benchmark in one unit, plus matching quantity, scope, and period. benchmark is the earlier or reference value; value is the later or actual value.
bestFor: target versus actual across several categories

recipes.data: At least 3 ordered labeled numeric values; 5 or more preferred.

recipes.purpose: Show dated policy, restriction, outage, contract, or operational intervals on a common calendar.
recipes.data: 2 to 8 labeled intervals with ISO start and end dates, or exact duration plus durationUnit when all intervals share timeline.anchorDate. Tone controls the interval color; displayValue names the duration.

recipes.purpose: Show parts of a whole when the shape of the composition matters.
Show exact parts of one total in a compact horizontal composition.
Explain how one exact reported quantity changes through same-period, same-scope additive steps into a reported ending amount.
recipes.data: 2 to 8 ordered items with role start, change, subtotal, or end; every item also needs reported valueStatus, period, and scope, and the values must reconcile.

recipes.purpose: Rank categories where labels need horizontal space.
Show a geographic breakdown across named continental administrative regions with collision-managed callout cards.
recipes.data: 1 to 12 items with a regionId or regionIds plus status, tone, value, or concise evidence.

composableFeatures.purpose: Add target, average, legal limit, prior norm, or other numeric reference lines without changing recipe.
Attach one short explanatory note to a specific data point or stage.
Use linear or logarithmic scale for extreme ratios.
Add up to four genuinely secondary contextual facts after a primary visual that already contains at least two quantitative or geographic marks. Supporting facts cannot be the chart.
Expose the tangible numerator and denominator behind a share or ratio, or the total population and affected count behind a risk estimate.
